sentences.text: This is first application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.370/2023 dated 6.10.2023 registered at Police Station - Jabera District - Damoh (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 498A, 304-B, 34 of IPC and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.

Applicant is in detention since 28.11.2023.
2.
As per the prosecution story, Neetu @ Mohini whose marriage was performed with Mousam Mehra in the in February 2017, committed suicide by consuming some poisonous substance.
It was alleged that she was being tortured and harassed by the husband and mother-in-law in connection with demand of a refrigerator and Rs.50,000/- cash.
FIR was registered.
After investigation, charge sheet has been filed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
She is innocent.
She has been falsely implicated.
Marriage was performed 6 years and 6 months ago and in this period, the deceased never made any complaint in writing before any authority about torture and harassment by mother-in-law and husband.
It is submitted that deceased was not keeping well and getting disappointed of her illness, she committed suicide.
Therefore, it is prayed that the applicant may be released on bail.

4 . O n the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the grant of bail to the applicant but learned counsel for the objector has submitted that he has no objection if applicant/
mother-in-law is released on bail..
5. Deceased has left two minor children behind her and there is no one to take care of those children.

Having taken into consideration the totality of allegations and facts and circumstances of the case, but without expressing anything on the merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pre-trial detention of the applicant is not warranted.
Consequently, this bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

6. It is directed that applicant -Smt. Anjani Mehra be released on bail on her furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for her regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that she shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

She shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
7 .
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case o f bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE mrs. mishra Smt. Anjani Mehra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85492572/
